{{Short description|American mathematician (born 1947)}}
'''Charles Robert Hadlock''' (born April 19, 1947, in [[Brooklyn]],<ref name=1970info>{{cite book|author=Hadlock, Charles Robert|title=Singular perturbations of a class of two point boundary value problems arising in optimal control|publisher=University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|year=1970}} (biographical information from preface to Ph.D. thesis)</ref> New York City) is an American applied mathematician, professor emeritus of mathematical sciences, and consultant in risk analysis. In 1985 he was awarded the inaugural [[Beckenbach Book Prize]] for his 1975 book ''Field theory and its classical problems''.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/0025570X.1985.11977151 |doi=10.1080/0025570X.1985.11977151 |title=MAA Awards, News & Letters |last1=Propp |first1=James |journal=Mathematics Magazine |volume=58 |issue=1 |page=57 |date=January 1985|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In July 2019 he was a George Póya Lecturer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/lecture-awards/pólya-lecturers |title=Pólya Lectures &#124; Mathematical Association of America }}</ref><ref name=Leadar>{{cite web|title=Charles Hadlock, George Pólya Lecturer at the Mathematical Association of America|website=Leadar|url=https://www.leadar.ai/profile/6287271395a814c6b4959f27}}</ref>

==Education and career==
In June 1964 Charles R. Hadlock graduated from Brooklyn's [[Xaverian High School]].<ref name=1970info/> In 1967 he received from [[Providence College]] a bachelor's degree in mathematics.<ref>{{cite book| title=University of Illinois (System), Transactions of the Board of Trustees, volume 58 | date=1968 |page=93 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TznVQtryzx4C&q=hadlock}}</ref> In 1970 he graduated from the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] with a Ph.D. in mathematics. His Ph.D. thesis ''Singular Perturbations of a Class of Two Point Boundary Value Problems Arising in Optimal Control'' was supervised by [[Petar V. Kokotovic]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=4790|name=Charles Robert Hadlock}}</ref> Hadlock was from 1970 to 1975 an assistant professor of mathematics at [[Amherst College]] and from 1976 to 1977 an assistant professor of mathematics at [[Bowdoin College]]. At the management consulting company [[Arthur D. Little]], he was from 1977 to 1979 a senior consultant and from 1979 to 1990 a manager in safety and environmental risk. After 13 years in corporate consulting, he became in 1990 a professor in mathematical sciences at [[Bentley University|Bentley College (renamed in 2008 Bentley University)]]. There he served as department chair and dean of the undergraduate college. He retired as professor emeritus in 2019.<ref name=Leadar/><ref name=homepage>{{cite web|website=Bentley University Faculty (faculty.bentley.edu)|title=Charlie Hadlock, Professor Emeritus, Mathematical Sciences|url=https://faculty.bentley.edu/profile/chadlock}}</ref> For the academic year 1996–1997 he was on leave of absence as a visiting professor of earth, atmospheric, and planetary sciences at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name=Leadar/>
 
Hadlock's research in applied mathematician involves risk analysis, agent-based simulations, environmental management, service-learning, and various forms of mathematical modeling. During his years with Arthur D. Little, Inc., he worked on environmental cases such as the [[Love Canal]] toxic chemical pollution, the [[Bhopal disaster]], and the [[Three Mile Island accident]]. His research and teaching dealt with mathematical models of stability of societal structures, economic and environmental changes, new forms of conflict, and bad leadership in the corporate and public sectors.<ref name=homepage/>

==Personal life==
In 1967, Hadlock married Joanne Theresa Miscione. They have a son and a daughter. For many years, during every summer there were family gatherings near a lake in Michigan. After raising their two children, Joanne earned a Ph.D. and became a licensed psychologist.<ref name=PiperShores>{{cite web|url=https://www.pipershores.org/blog/piper-personalities-meet-the-hadlocks-and-giasis/ |date=March 6, 2023|title=Piper Personalities: Meet the Hadlock's & the Giasi's|website=Piper Shores Lifecare Community }}</ref> She also wrote a book ''Yard Sale Savvy: The Ultimate Guide to Bargains, Treasures, and Fun'', published in 2011.<ref>{{cite book|title=Yard Sale Savvy: The Ultimate Guide to Bargains, Treasures, and Fun|year=2011|author=Hadlock, Joanne|publisher=Sandy Pond Press|postscript=; pbk, 142 pages|isbn=978-0983285007}}</ref> In 2021, Charles and Joanne Hadlock retired to an oceanside community in [[Scarborough, Maine]].<ref name=PiperShores/>
